title: run_all.ipynb

canonical_node.axiom: The complete Theophysics test suite must be executable in a single Colab session by any user with a Google account, producing reproducible outputs.
definitions: run_all.ipynb: a Google Colab notebook that executes all project notebooks in a defined sequence.
Complete test suite: all JAX field theory tests (1A, 1B, 2A, 2B, 3, 4, 5) and all biblical empirical tests (03-09).
Reproducible: the same inputs and code produce the same outputs, verified by SHA256 checksums.
derivation: The document states that run_all.ipynb executes all notebooks in a specific order.
It claims that running all cells produces full console output, JSON result files, PNG charts, a summary JSON, and SHA256 checksums.
It asserts that this makes the framework reproducible by anyone, not just the author.
It equates this to a repeatable experiment protocol.
canonical_node.action: Execute all project notebooks in the specified sequence within a single Colab session, producing all outputs and verifying reproducibility via checksums.
boundary: Does not itself contain the scientific content of the tests; it orchestrates their execution.
Does not guarantee that the tests pass; it only executes them and reports results.
Does not provide a formal proof of the underlying physics; it is a computational runner.
test: Run the notebook in a fresh Colab instance and verify that all cells execute without error.
Check that all expected output files (JSON, PNG, summary) are generated.
Verify that the SHA256 checksums match the expected values for reproducibility.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a one-button execution mechanism that allows any user to run the entire test suite without manual setup, enabling independent verification.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the ability to run each individual test notebook independently, as the runner simply orchestrates them.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without run_all.ipynb, the claim of easy reproducibility by anyone is weakened; users would need to manually run each notebook in sequence, increasing friction and potential for error.

overstatement_risks: The document claims that running the notebook reproduces the complete proof, but the proof itself is not established; it only reproduces the test suite execution.
The phrase 'computational equivalent of repeatable experiment protocol' may overstate the scientific validity of the tests.
kill_conditions: If the notebook fails to execute in a fresh Colab environment due to missing dependencies or code errors.
If the checksums do not match, indicating non-reproducibility.
risk.lean_target: A script that executes all tests and produces a summary report, without claiming proof of the underlying theory.

plain_summary: run_all.ipynb is a master notebook that runs all Theophysics tests in one go, aiming to make the framework easy to reproduce. It is an operational tool, not a proof of the theory itself.
